transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Vice President J.D. Vance called out Republicans who've been criticizing fellow GOP candidate
for Ohio Governor Vivek Ramaswamy for an ad he ran against his Democratic opponent, Amy
Acton.
I have to admit that I'm a little bit disgusted when I see Republicans across the country
who are whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional
Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America.
The advertisement features Acton's estranged mother calling her a liar.
Acton's stepfather was charged with raping her when she was 12.
During a visit near Cincinnati today, Vance said politics is a tough business.
The top Democrats on the Senate and House Intelligence Committee say that while foreign
powers are attempting to influence U.S. elections, they have not seen evidence that any nation
is trying to actually interfere in the voting process itself, and PR's Eric McDaniel has
this report.
Senator Mark Warner tells NPR that Russia, similar to prior occasions, is going after
Democrats with misinformation.
He says Iran is looking more at disruption in Europe and that China has focused on local
races or smaller issues with Chinese nationals involved.
The ranking intel member on the House side, Congressman Jim Haim, says that there is a
profound distinction between those influence campaigns and actual interference in election
infrastructure itself.
Haim also emphasizes that, quote, "We've never seen an operation to actually interfere.
And as of now, we're not seeing either the capability or the intent to interfere."
Both men say they've told Trump's intel heads that they need to be reachable by phone
and ready to provide evidence if the administration claims election fraud tied to foreign meddling.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Washington.
A serious security vulnerability in a popular programming language has website operators
around the world scrambling to protect their web pages.
News outlets to government agencies could be affected, as NPR's Jenna McLaughlin reports.
The language, called PHP, quietly supports components of major platforms like WordPress
and Drupal.
Some estimates suggest PHP is used to power close to 70 percent of modern web pages.
Government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland, for example, took their websites
offline to preempt any attacks.
Major technology companies were involved in uncovering the flaw, including OpenAI, which
said in a blog post that its model helped find the bug before attackers did.
Developers maintaining the programming language released patches to seal the hole on Wednesday.
The NSA urged organizations to take their systems down and apply the fix immediately.
Jenna McLaughlin, NPR News.
The Trump administration is asking the Supreme Court to let it resume building a border wall
through Texas' Big Bend region.
A lower court had halted construction, a setback to one of President Trump's key projects,
ranchers, residents and environmentalists in Big Bend opposed the project, citing low
illegal immigration in the area.
The administration has been pushing forward with the wall from the Pacific Ocean to the
Gulf of Mexico.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
New Mexico's Democratic Attorney General is suing Jeffrey Epstein's former attorney
and accountant.
The lawsuit accuses Darren Indike and Richard Kahn of concealing the disgraced financier's
alleged sex trafficking operation at his ranch near Santa Fe.
The lawsuit also seeks to stop them from accepting any payments from Epstein's estate.
New research in the journal Science Advances suggests that a common vaccine for tuberculosis
may help protect against some forms of dementia, and Piers Pinkwong reports.
The BCG vaccine is used to prevent tuberculosis.
It's also used as a treatment for bladder cancer, and patients who receive it are less
likely to develop Alzheimer's disease.
Dr. William Bichai at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine wanted to know why.
So he and his colleagues turned to lab mice engineered to show symptoms of the disease.
To some, they gave high doses of the vaccine, then the mice took memory tests.
The ones that weren't vaccinated did poorly.
They got C minuses, you know, and the vaccinated ones performed at the same level as a healthy
non-diseased mouse.
The vaccinated mice also had less protein buildup and inflammation in the brain.
Bichai says there's much work ahead, but he hopes the vaccine's long safety profile
can help speed up clinical trials in humans.
Pinkwong, NPR News.
The Glacier Garden in Lucerne is showcasing artifacts from Switzerland's glaciers, an
exhibit called "Treasury of Ice."
The exhibit features relics like an ancient bow, a Roman statuette, and an alpinist's
helmet.
The museum director says the exhibit aims to highlight the importance of these artifacts
before the glaciers disappear.
I'm Rylan Barton.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Vance criticizes GOP attacks on Vivek Ramaswamy's ad against Democrat Amy Acton
Senate and House intel leaders say foreign powers are influencing but not interfering with US elections
Serious PHP programming language flaw prompts websites worldwide to patch or go offline
Trump administration asks Supreme Court to resume border wall construction in Texas Big Bend region
New Mexico attorney general sues Jeffrey Epstein's former attorney and accountant Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn
Study suggests tuberculosis BCG vaccine may protect against Alzheimer's disease in lab mice
Lucerne Glacier Garden exhibit 'Treasury of Ice' displays artifacts from melting Swiss glaciers
